examples.title: Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component
examples.description:
This example demonstrates the basic usage of the WaterFlow component, including data loading, attribute setting, and event callbacks.
WaterFlowDataSource implements the LazyForEach data source API IDataSource, which is used to provide child components for WaterFlow through LazyForEach.

examples.title: Example 2: Implementing Automatic Column Count Calculation
examples.description:
This example showcases how to implement automatic column count calculation using the auto-fill feature.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 3: Using WaterFlowSections
examples.description:
This example illustrates the initialization of WaterFlowSections and the different effects of various APIs such as splice, push, update, values, and length.
For usage with state management V2, see WaterFlow and makeObserved.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 4: Using the Pinch Gesture to Change the Column Count
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to use priorityGesture and PinchGesture to implement the feature of using a pinch gesture to change the number of columns in a layout.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 5: Setting the Edge Fading Effect
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to enable the edge fading effect for the WaterFlow component using the fadingEdge API and set the length of the fading edge using the fadingEdgeLength parameter.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 6: Setting the Single-Side Edge Effect
examples.description:
This example uses the edgeEffect API to set the single-side edge effect for the WaterFlow component.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 7: Setting and Changing the Footer Component in the WaterFlow Component
examples.description:
In API version 18 and later versions, this example demonstrates how to set the footer component in the WaterFlow component using the footerContent API of WaterFlowOptions. The footer component is updated using the update function of ComponentContent.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 8: Implementing Pull-to-Refresh for a WaterFlow Component
examples.description:
This example demonstrates how to implement the pull-to-fresh function for the data source of the WaterFlow component via Refresh.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 9: Configuring the Number of Columns in the WaterFlow Component Based on Breakpoints
examples.description: In API version 22 and later versions, this example shows how to configure the number of columns in the WaterFlow component based on breakpoints.

examples.title: Example 10: Obtaining the Content Height for the WaterFlow Component
examples.description:
From API version 22, this example uses the WaterFlow component to obtain the content height.
For details about WaterFlowDataSource and the complete code, see Example 1: Using a Basic WaterFlow Component.

examples.title: Example 11: Setting a Scrolling Event
examples.description:
This example obtains a UIWaterFlowEvent instance via getEvent('WaterFlow') on a FrameNode and sets scroll event callbacks for a WaterFlow component. This approach is intended for scenarios where the page code cannot be directly modified to use declarative callbacks.
The UIWaterFlowEvent API is added since API version 19.
